# Synthetic data


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A task’s synthetic inputs should cover every kind of case the model must
handle, not drift towards the common ones. Following [synthetic
questions for
MARIS](https://fr.anckalbi.net/posts/synthetic-questions-maris/), we
list the *dimensions* along which cases vary, give each a few *levels*,
and sample *tuples*: combinations of one level from each dimension. Each
tuple stands for one distinct kind of case. This module holds the part
every task shares; each task supplies its own dimensions and a generator
that turns a tuple into one input.

## Tuples

Dimensions are a dict from dimension name to its levels. The MARIS
dimensions make a small example:

``` python
maris = dict(purpose=['scientific', 'regulatory', 'educational', 'metadata'],
             audience=['domain expert', 'professional', 'general public'],
             complexity=['direct factual', 'analytical', 'conceptual'])
```

### tuples

``` python
def tuples(
    dims:dict, # Dimension name -> its levels
)->list[dict]:
```

*All combinations of levels, one from each dimension*

There are 4 × 3 × 3 = 36 tuples:

``` python
ts = tuples(maris)
test_eq(len(ts), 36)
ts[:2]
```

    [{'purpose': 'scientific',
      'audience': 'domain expert',
      'complexity': 'direct factual'},
     {'purpose': 'scientific',
      'audience': 'domain expert',
      'complexity': 'analytical'}]

## Sampling

[`sample`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/synth.html#sample)
calls the task’s generator `gen(tuple, rng)` `n` times. It cycles
through the tuples in a shuffled order, so each tuple gets
`n // len(tuples)` inputs or one more: 270 inputs over 27 tuples gives
exactly 10 each, and 50 inputs gives 1 or 2 each. All randomness comes
from one `random.Random(seed)` passed to the generator, so a seed
reproduces the whole set. Different seeds give the independent draws
needed for separate training and test sets.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/franckalbinet/edgeslm/blob/main/edgeslm/synth.py#L21"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### sample

``` python
def sample(
    dims:dict, # Dimension name -> its levels
    gen, # `gen(tuple, rng)` returns one input for `tuple`
    n:int, # Number of inputs
    seed:int=0, # Seed of the random generator passed to `gen`
)->list[dict]: # Dicts with the `tuple` and the generated `input`
```

*`n` inputs from `gen`, spread evenly over the tuples of `dims`*

A generator for MARIS would ask a model for a question; this one only
builds a placeholder string:

``` python
def placeholder(t, rng): return f"{t['complexity']} {t['purpose']} question for the {t['audience']} (#{rng.randint(1, 99)})"

recs = sample(maris, placeholder, 72, seed=1)
recs[0]
```

    {'tuple': {'purpose': 'metadata',
      'audience': 'general public',
      'complexity': 'analytical'},
     'input': 'analytical metadata question for the general public (#68)'}

Every tuple appears twice in 72 inputs, and the same seed gives the same
inputs:

``` python
test_eq(set(Counter(tuple(r['tuple'].values()) for r in recs).values()), {2})
test_eq(sample(maris, placeholder, 72, seed=1), recs)
```
